title: Which Chatbots Best Resist Propaganda?
hook: Estonia put dozens of AI models to the test: when nudged toward Russia's talking points, which ones held the line? It turns out the chatbot you choose can shape the slant of what you're told.
key_points: An Estonian government benchmark scored dozens of LLMs on resisting Russian 'strategic narratives.'
Models varied — some pushed back on propaganda framings, others absorbed and repeated them.
Chatbots learn from the internet, so they can pick up and echo coordinated disinformation.
Takeaway: on contested topics, which model you ask — and cross-checking — actually matters.
content_html: On June 4, 2026, Ars Technica covered an unusual benchmark from Estonia's government: a test of how dozens of large language models hold up when prompted toward Russia's "strategic narratives" — the framings and talking points behind state propaganda. The headline finding is that models differ. Some consistently pushed back or added context; others more readily absorbed and repeated the propaganda framing.
extra_html: Why would a chatbot parrot propaganda at all? Because these systems learn by digesting enormous amounts of text from the open internet, and that text includes deliberate, coordinated disinformation. A model has no independent sense of geopolitical truth; it reflects patterns in what it was trained on and how it was tuned. The practical lesson for an everyday user is quieter than the geopolitics: on any contested or politically charged topic, the specific AI you ask can tilt the answer, and treating a single chatbot as a neutral oracle is a mistake. Cross-check against accountable sources, and remember that "the AI said so" is not the same as "it's true."

related.title: What Happens to Truth?
related.hook: When anything can be faked and the internet floods with synthetic everything, the danger isn't just believing lies — it's the 'liar's dividend,' where real evidence gets dismissed as fake too.

related.title: When AI Makes Things Up
related.hook: AI 'hallucinations' aren't glitches — they're the technology working as designed. A model that always predicts a plausible next word will sometimes produce a plausible falsehood.

related.title: AI & the News
related.hook: AI now writes news, fakes whole 'outlets,' and powers the feed deciding what you see. Staying informed increasingly means knowing how the sausage is made — and who made it.
